## Executive summary

This generalist review read the entire OWASP NodeGoat tree end to end
(/root/targets/NodeGoat, 111 files locked by SHA-256): every Express route
(`app/routes/*.js`), every data-access module (`app/data/*.js`), all configuration
(`config/`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `.github/workflows/`), every view
(`app/views/**/*.html`), and the client-side JavaScript (`app/assets/js/**`).
NodeGoat is a deliberately vulnerable teaching app whose canonical defects (NoSQL
injection, `eval()` on request input, plaintext password comparison, a hard-coded
session-cookie secret, global autoescape disabled, CSRF protection commented out,
IDOR on `/benefits` and `/allocations/:userId`) each fall squarely inside one of the
six specialist departments reading this same tree in parallel, so this report does
not restate them. It carries 3 findings, all medium severity, chosen because they
either fall outside the vocabulary any of the six specialist skills names, or sit at
a line a single-subject read would plausibly skip: (1) an unvalidated open redirect
on `/learn` (app/routes/index.js:72); (2) the entire merged application config,
secrets included, printed to stdout on every process start
(config/config.js:12-13); (3) an in-memory session store that creates a stored
session for every visitor, authenticated or not, with no expiry, enabling memory
exhaustion (server.js:78-85). Method: entry points read first, one finding per
sink, the exact line quoted and verified, `semgrep` run with the local rule pack
plus `p/owasp-top-ten` as a lead generator rather than as proof.

- critical: 0
- high: 0
- medium: 3
- low: 0
- info: 0

## Scope and method

Target: `/root/targets/NodeGoat`, the exact 111 files and SHA-256 digests locked in
`target.json` (root SHA-256 `78ac112b7bd5083bb065086c4642dcd8a3932a8d3052f9405503124c90a70fe3`).
Every route handler, DAO, config file, Dockerfile/Compose/CI file, and HTML view was
opened and read; `app/assets/vendor/**` (third-party JS/CSS bundles) and binary
assets (fonts, images) were located but not read line-by-line since they carry no
first-party logic. `semgrep 1.177.0` was run once over the whole tree with
`--config /home/user/deepseek-harness/examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/program-code-safety/semgrep --config p/owasp-top-ten --metrics off --json`
(29 results, plus 10 template-parsing errors on `.html` files that use Nunjucks/Swig
syntax semgrep's Jinja parser does not accept); every hit was read at its source
location and treated as a lead, never as a finding on its own. Method follows the
`review-method` skill: entry points enumerated first (`app/routes/index.js`), data
traced from each attacker-controlled input to its sink, one finding per sink, exact
line quoted and mechanically re-verified against the locked tree with
`verify-safety-report.mjs`. This department's mandate is the whole application
across every defect class, specifically to surface what a single-subject read would
not; findings that squarely match one of the access/data/dependencies/injection/
platform/secrets departments' own named subjects were deliberately left for that
department and are not repeated here even where they were read and confirmed during
this pass.

## Findings

### medium

- `generalist-open-redirect-learn` — The /learn route redirects to any attacker-supplied URL with no validation (`app/routes/index.js:72`, CWE-601, confirmed) — an authenticated-but-unchecked open redirect usable for phishing; fix by allowlisting or removing client control of the destination.
- `generalist-secrets-console-dump` — The merged application config, including the session and crypto secrets, is printed to stdout on every startup (`config/config.js:12-13`, CWE-532, confirmed) — secrets leak into whatever log pipeline captures process stdout; fix by removing or redacting this log line.
- `generalist-session-memorystore-dos` — express-session is mounted with the default in-memory store, saveUninitialized:true, and no cookie expiry, so every visit leaks a session that is never pruned (`server.js:78-85`, CWE-770, likely) — unauthenticated memory-exhaustion DoS; fix with a bounded external session store, saveUninitialized:false, and an explicit cookie.maxAge.

## What was not covered

- The six specialist departments' own subjects were deliberately not restated here even when confirmed while reading: NoSQL injection via `$where` in `app/data/allocations-dao.js:78` (injection), `eval()` on request input in `app/routes/contributions.js:32-34` (injection), plaintext password storage and `===` comparison in `app/data/user-dao.js:25,61` (access/data), the hard-coded `cookieSecret`/`cryptoKey` in `config/env/all.js:8-9` (secrets), global Swig `autoescape: false` in `server.js:137` and the resulting XSS surface across `app/views/**` (injection), CSRF protection commented out in `server.js:105-113` (access), missing `isAdmin` check on `POST /benefits` in `app/routes/index.js:55-56` and the IDOR on `GET /allocations/:userId` in `app/routes/allocations.js` (access), missing security headers / helmet commented out in `server.js:38-65` (platform), and the `mongodb`/`swig`/`marked`/`node-esapi` pinned-but-old dependencies in `package.json` (dependencies).
- SSRF in `app/routes/research.js:15-16` was read and is real, but it is the application's own labeled A10/SSRF tutorial example and squarely the injection department's named subject (SSRF), so it is not repeated as a generalist finding.
- `app/assets/vendor/**` (bundled third-party bootstrap/jquery/morris/font-awesome) was enumerated but not read line-by-line; these are unmodified upstream bundles, not first-party code.
- No dynamic testing, dependency-vulnerability database lookup, or `npm audit` was run in this pass; the `dependencies` department covers that separately.
- Runtime/deployment behavior (actual environment variables, network topology, a WAF, or whatever log aggregator is really attached to the container's stdout) could not be confirmed from static reading alone; the impact of `generalist-secrets-console-dump` depends on which log sink is really attached in a given deployment.
- The `generalist-session-memorystore-dos` finding is `likely`, not `confirmed`, because MemoryStore's unbounded-growth behavior is documented library behavior, not something read from this repository's own source (`express-session` is a dependency, not part of the locked target tree).

## Certificate

Verified findings: 3
Target tree: 78ac112b7bd5083bb065086c4642dcd8a3932a8d3052f9405503124c90a70fe3

`node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings findings/generalist.json` mechanically confirmed that all 3 findings resolve to a real file and line in the locked tree, that all 3 ids are unique, and that no two findings share file, line, and CWE.

This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".
"}

## Summary

I reviewed the OWASP NodeGoat target tree (`/root/targets/NodeGoat`, 111 files locked by `target.json`) end to end — every route, DAO, config file, Dockerfile/Compose/CI file, view template, and client-side script — before deciding what to report, per the generalist mandate.

**Semgrep**: ran `semgrep --config .../semgrep --config p/owasp-top-ten --metrics off --json .` (v1.177.0, 29 results) and treated every hit as a lead to read, not a finding.

Since NodeGoat is a deliberately vulnerable teaching app, nearly everything obvious (NoSQL `$where` injection, `eval()` on request input, plaintext password comparison, hard-coded `cookieSecret`, global `autoescape: false` XSS surface, CSRF disabled, missing `isAdmin` checks / IDOR, missing security headers, outdated pinned dependencies) falls squarely inside one of the six specialist departments' named subjects, so I deliberately left those for them and looked instead for defects that fall *between* the six skills' explicit vocabularies. I delivered 3 findings, all `medium` severity:

1. **`generalist-open-redirect-learn`** (CWE-601, confirmed) — `app/routes/index.js:72` redirects to an unvalidated `req.query.url`. Open redirect isn't named by any of the six subject skills (injection lists SSRF/path-traversal but not open redirect; access/platform don't mention it either).
2. **`generalist-secrets-console-dump`** (CWE-532, confirmed) — `config/config.js:12-13` dumps the entire merged config, including `cookieSecret`/`cryptoKey`, to stdout on every process start — a distinct logging-pipeline sink from the secret's literal in source.
3. **`generalist-session-memorystore-dos`** (CWE-770, likely) — `server.js:78-85` mounts `express-session` with the default unbounded MemoryStore, `saveUninitialized: true`, and no `cookie.maxAge`, letting any anonymous visitor leak a never-pruned server-side session.

All three were mechanically verified with `node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings findings/generalist.json` (passes), and both `findings/generalist.json` and `report/generalist.md` are committed on the department branch `safety/program-.../generalist` (commit `d84122d`), with a clean working tree.
